name: Lakehouse (Iceberg on AWS Glue)

companions.name: LAKEHOUSE_DISTRIBUTE_FILES
companions.body:
function run(ctx)
    repeat
        ctx.emit(ctx.files)
    until not ctx.next()
end

inputs.name: region
inputs.label: AWS region of the Glue catalog and its bucket (e.g. eu-central-1)

inputs.name: database
inputs.label: Glue database (one database is one virtual schema)

inputs.name: access_key_id
inputs.label: Access key ID (Enter if the credential file holds it)

access: glue:GetDatabase, GetTables, GetTable and GetPartitions on the database and its tables, s3:ListBucket on the table locations and s3:GetObject on their objects
tips: Names arrive in upper case (ORDERS, ORDER_ID): no quotes needed.
notes: Reads the Iceberg tables of one AWS Glue database (and its plain Hive Parquet tables) where they lie in S3: exasol-labs' lakehouse-engine-rs runs Apache DataFusion inside the Rust language container (the same 0.33.0 container MongoDB uses). Iceberg deletes are applied (positional and deletion vectors); equality deletes, ORC and Avro are refused by name.
The release is a .tar.gz pinned per CPU; the .so inside it is pinned too, and staged only when both match.

The adapter calls its companion scripts by fixed names in its own schema (LAKEHOUSE_SCAN, LAKEHOUSE_DISTRIBUTE_FILES; LAKEHOUSE_VERSION reports the build), so every lakehouse source shares them, like MongoDB's.

Measured live (v0.57.3, Glue in ap-south-1, Athena-written Iceberg v2 tables with a DELETE and an UPDATE): counts, sums, a partition filter and a join equal Athena's answers; the same tables through Glue's Iceberg REST endpoint read identically. The pushdown and the schema's properties carry the CONNECTION's name, never a key.

Credentials are an IAM access key pair (or the JSON `aws iam create-access-key` prints) in the CONNECTION's password, as JSON; the engine signs Glue and S3 requests with it. A database the key may not read - or one that does not exist, under a scoped policy - is refused as AccessDenied.
